_comment: Equipment code -> what is actually in the cabin. This table exists because a feed giving an equipment code has NOT told you the cabin: hard rule 2 in table form. Duffel and Amadeus return aircraft.code ('789'), which names a TYPE. One carrier's 789 may be two or three configurations with two or three connectivity systems, and the frame is swapped after booking anyway. So every row here is a HEDGED CLAIM with a frequency, never a fact, and a type with no row still abstains rather than being guessed from the type alone.
_source: Published sources per row (airline fleet pages, reports and press releases where readable; Airbus Orders & Deliveries; aeroLOPA seat maps; dated aviation press), each figure re-checked by a second reader
_what_the_frequency_is: The SHARE OF THE CARRIER'S FRAMES of that type that carry the described configuration, which is the MOST COMMON one, with sample_size the number of frames. A tail is assigned close to departure, so that share is close to the chance any one departure gets that cabin, and a low share really is a coin flip. (Until 2026-09-25 the rows named the BETTER configuration instead, which made a type with one refitted jet in twenty read as a coin flip.) It is NOT a count of departures. Wifi rows give the share of frames with wifi that works over the ocean; 'No wifi' rows carry outcome false.
_review: CHECKED 2026-09-25: every row was researched against published, dated sources (four researchers) and every figure re-checked by a second reader who opened the sources; their corrections are applied and kept under each row's _evidence.second_check. needs_primary_source stays true where no airline or manufacturer source backs the row (many airline fleet pages refuse automated readers, so aeroLOPA and the press carry the count), or where confidence was low. A row with no published split, or no published wifi count, ABSTAINS rather than guessing. AZ:333 and OS:77W were removed (the airlines no longer fly the type) and EY:359 became EY:351 (Etihad flies the A350-1000). Refits move monthly: re-check the rows whose _evidence names a refit in progress.
_keying: CARRIER:EQUIPMENT, on the OPERATING carrier - the metal belongs to whoever flies it, not to whoever sold it.
_scope: Transatlantic long-haul types for the carriers a real JFK-LHR search returns, plus the narrowbodies that feed their European hubs. A short-haul row exists so a feeder segment is not abstain-priced; the connectivity term is only charged on the longest segment of an itinerary.
